_meta.indication: XOLREMDI is indicated in patients 12 years of age and older with WHIM syndrome (warts, hypogammaglobulinemia, infections and myelokathexis) to increase the number of circulating mature neutrophils and lymphocytes.

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled registrational trial (randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized 1:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 52-week study; stratified by prophylactic immunoglobulin (IgG) use
pivotal_trials.population: Adults and adolescents ≥12 years of age with WHIM syndrome, with a genotype-confirmed CXCR4 variant and confirmed ANC ≤400 cells/µL
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: mean time above threshold for absolute neutrophil count (TAT_ANC) of 500 cells/µL over a 24-hour period
pivotal_trials.result: TAT_ANC was statistically significantly greater with XOLREMDI (LS mean 15.0 hours) vs placebo (2.8 hours); LS mean difference 12.3 hours (95% CI 7.2, 17.4), p<0.0001. First secondary TAT_ALC also positive: XOLREMDI 15.8 vs placebo 4.6 hours, p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were thrombocytopenia (21%), pityriasis, rash, rhinitis, epistaxis, vomiting, and dizziness (each 14%). Serious adverse reactions of thrombocytopenia occurred in 3 of 14 XOLREMDI patients.
target_moa: Mavorixafor is an orally bioavailable CXCR4 antagonist that blocks the binding of the CXCR4 ligand SDF-1α/CXCL12; gain-of-function CXCR4 mutations in WHIM patients lead to retention of leukocytes in the bone marrow, and treatment with mavorixafor results in increased mobilization of neutrophils and lymphocytes from the bone marrow into peripheral circulation.
modality: Small molecule (orally bioavailable CXCR4 antagonist, capsules)
companion_dx_detail: No FDA-approved companion diagnostic is required; enrolled patients had a genotype-confirmed CXCR4 variant consistent with WHIM syndrome but the label does not name a companion diagnostic test.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an Advisory Committee meeting because it did not raise efficacy, safety or public health questions requiring advice from external experts.

summary.text: XOLREMDI received a full (traditional) priority-review NDA approval for WHIM syndrome, supported by orphan drug designation (October 10, 2018), breakthrough therapy designation (November 8, 2019), and fast track designation (October 1, 2020); it was also granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. It was not an accelerated approval and was not referred to an advisory committee.
